To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Malaysian ESL syllabus and examination are very different in their constructs.

the Malaysian English language curriculum document and high stakes examination papers are not congruent in terms of their constructs, and the examination construct has greater congruence with the beliefs and pedagogical skills of teachers.

the ESL syllabus and examination do not share similar specifications, teachers’ cognitions and beliefs are more aligned with the examination specifications, and teachers are likely to follow the construct and specifications of the examination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the washback of examinations and syllabi in the classroom.
understanding the washback effects of the syllabus and the examination on the classroom practices of teachers.
the relationship between the examination and the syllabus, and the effects of this relationship in the classroom.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
teachers’ beliefs and their pedagogic skills play an important role in determining the extent and nature of washback.
the syllabus and the examination do not share similar language constructs.
the examination construct is more dominant in the teaching of English in Malaysian schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the syllabus and exam are not in sync with each other.
teachers are aware of the differences between the two and that they tend to follow the examination construct in their teaching because of their beliefs and pedagogical competencies.
the examination is the dominant factor that shapes the classroom practice in ESL classrooms in Malaysia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construct of the syllabus and that of the examination should match, so that teachers can focus on the syllabus and not on the examination.
teachers’ cognitions and decision making are influenced by the constructs of the curriculum documents and the examination papers.
the syllabus document does not have any influence over teachers' teaching practices.
